Application Areas: Smart City Surveillance and Urban Security Management
Privacy-Preserving Biometric and Edge Computing Services
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Privacy-Preserving Federated Unlearning: Implementing client-level selective erasure and local differential privacy to mitigate data poisoning and ensure model unlearning as a service (UaaS) in distributed edge networks.

Multi-Agent Reinforcement Optimization: Utilizing Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) to dynamically optimize UAV trajectories, task offloading, and RIS phase shifts in complex aerial-edge environments.

Digital Twin-Integrated Security Frameworks: Leveraging Digital Twin Technology to simulate and mitigate adversarial attacks, such as DeepFool and gradient-based loss maximization, on facial recognition and surveillance datasets.

Cooperative Aerial-Ground Resource Allocation: Applying Game Theory and Differential Evolution (DE) to coordinate wireless energy transfer (WET) and beamforming between High-Altitude Platforms (HAPs), UAVs, and Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGVs) for energy-efficient communication.
Summary Description: Mohammad Atiquzzaman specializes in securing and optimizing next-generation 6G wireless communications, bridging AI-driven security with resilient infrastructure. His work addresses critical vulnerabilities in Federated Learning via Digital Twin-integrated Unlearning and adversarial biometric protection. Expanding into disaster response and urban monitoring, he pioneers aerial-edge computing frameworks integrating High-Altitude Platforms (HAPs), UAVs, and Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGVs). By leveraging Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL), Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), and Genetic Algorithms (GA), he optimizes UAV trajectories, RIS states, and task offloading. He further introduces UAV-UGV cooperative systems using Differential Evolution (DE) for RIS configuration and wireless energy beamforming, ensuring low-latency, energy-efficient, and reliable communication for ground devices in compromised or dense urban environments.
